candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7/PDF p.11: Collaborate with members of the interprofessional health care team to facilitate client care; Participate in client care coordination; Participate in performance improvement activities
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — team debriefing and performance improvement
candidate.educational_objective: Use a TeamSTEPPS debrief after a clinical event to review team performance, identify lessons, reinforce effective behaviors, and plan improvements for future care.

options.A: Establish team membership, roles, goals, and the care plan before the procedure begins.
options.B: Re-establish situational awareness and modify the care plan during an evolving clinical situation.
options.C: Verify that a specific communicated message was heard and understood correctly through closed-loop communication.
options.D: Review what occurred, identify what worked and what did not, reinforce successes, and use lessons learned to improve future team performance.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS defines a debrief as a post-event review focused on recounting key events, analyzing what worked and what did not, identifying lessons learned, reinforcing successful behaviors, and improving the plan for future cases. Therefore D is correct. A describes a brief, B describes a huddle, and C describes a check-back rather than a debrief.
candidate.source_claim_supported: TeamSTEPPS debriefs are post-event performance-improvement reviews that examine key events, successes, problems, lessons learned, and changes for future cases; briefs are pre-care planning, huddles reassess the plan during care, and check-backs verify communicated information.
candidate.source_document_title: TeamSTEPPS 3.0 — Reviewing the Team's Performance: Debrief
